title: Rehearsal: run every built governance mechanism end to end in a throwaway copy
description: The 2026-10-07 review counted 6 built mechanisms with 0 real uses (contest, phase B yield, acts signed by fedatarios, delegated credentials with a ceiling, cases resolved by citing a rule, sovereignty KPI measurements). Build examples/rehearsal/run_rehearsal.py: it copies the harness into a temporary directory, drives one connected scenario through the tools' own CLIs only, and prints a scorecard per mechanism (fired / blocked / unbuilt) whose every fired entry points at evidence the tool itself wrote. The live .harness is never written. Nothing is signed with the operator's key and no warrant is signed.
acceptance_criteria: examples/rehearsal/run_rehearsal.py copies the harness into a fresh temporary directory and runs there; the live repository is never written: git status --porcelain and a sha256 of every file under .harness/ (excluding logs/ and the T-440 task file) are identical before and after a run.
The scenario is driven only through the tools' command lines (subprocess), never by importing their internals, so it proves the tools as an adopter meets them.

The scenario is ONE connected story, not 12 isolated calls: the same names, tasks and records flow from one act to the next (a worker's task is verified, a dispute about it becomes a case, the case is deliberated and disposed by a published precedent, a later case is disposed by citing that precedent, and so on).

It attempts each mechanism and records an outcome for each: producer-not-approver refusal; handoff and a distinct verifier's verdict; a case opened and deliberated (propose, sponsor, prior, discuss, vote, conclude, Condorcet) by at least 3 distinct names; a precedent published disposing it; a SECOND case disposed by citing that precedent (visible in precedent.py disposition-ratio); a confirmation by a distinct author; a phase B yield (event phase_b_yield) from blackboard.py next; an act signed by a fedatario seat holder and verified; a delegation with a ceiling used within it and refused beyond it; a fork under one name detected by attest.py forks and contested by a different name on its own chain, with the contested act carrying no weight; currency.py and event_stats.py reading the sandbox; westphalia_kpi.py attempted with a second registry; contracts and breach (decision 2) reported as designed, not built.

Scorecard: printed and written as JSON. Each mechanism is fired, blocked or unbuilt. A fired entry names the evidence the TOOL wrote (event name and line in the sandbox events log, act file, case file, precedent id). Printed text alone never counts. A blocked entry names what blocks it (a missing ratified record, a pending operator decision, a tool refusal) with the tool's own message. No mechanism is faked or simulated by writing its evidence directly.

Security: no warrant is signed; ~/.ssh/harness_root is never read; nothing under the live .harness/keys is read or copied. Public trust material and the constitutional payload and signature may be copied into the sandbox so phase B verifies there. Any agent key the scenario needs is generated inside the temporary directory and dies with it.
A test in .harness/tests runs the rehearsal in a temporary directory and asserts: every fired entry has tool-written evidence, and the live tree is untouched. Full suite passes via goal_mode.py run.
No absolute user paths in code, comments, output or board notes. Hand off to role verifier; never self-mark done.

Scenario ("Casona", one connected story, same names/tasks/records throughout, driven
only via subprocess onto each tool's own CLI -- see docstring for the full chain):
FIRED (8): producer-not-approver refusal; handoff + distinct verifier done; a case
  (precedent.py case open) deliberated end to end (deliberate.py propose/sponsor x2/
  prior/schedule/discuss x2/vote x5/conclude --method schulze, 5 distinct names,
  Condorcet winner) and disposed by a published precedent; a confirmation by a
  distinct author; a second case disposed by publish --follows (visible in the
  first record's own cited_by and in disposition-ratio's by_legislation_registered;
  the narrower by_citation/`distinguish` path was attempted and is one of the
  blocked findings below); a phase_b_yield event from blackboard.py next (the
  outranking identity's score traces to this run's own precedent authorship +
  confirmation + citation); currency.py and event_stats.py reading the sandbox.
BLOCKED (4), all four reducing to ONE root cause, each with the tool's own message:
  attest.py's D3a intent gate (open_intents()) requires an intent SIGNED AND
  VERIFIED against a name's WARRANT-RECORDED key before any privileged act (grant,
  distinguish, contest, verdict); this rehearsal is barred from reading the live
  private key under .harness/keys/ and barred from signing a warrant to mint one it
  would hold, so no privileged act can originate from an already-warranted name.
  (1) fedatario sign+verify: a non-privileged `commit` act DOES sign (fed-codificador
      is warrant-enrolled in the sandbox's copy of the already-signed, public W-002),
      but attest.py verify reports a signature failure -- sign_act never checks the
      signing key against the warrant's recorded pubkey, only verify does.
  (2) delegation ceiling: the grant itself is refused at the intent-match step.
  (3) fork+contest: 2 genuinely concurrent `attest.py sign` CLI calls (threading)
      produced ZERO forks (roster._guard now serializes read-decide-create-write,
      confirmed live rather than only in the test suite); contest was attempted
      regardless and refused at the same intent gate.
  (4) westphalia_kpi.py: domain_registries() hardcodes exactly one candidate
      registry ({'precedents':'PR-'}); reports NOT YET MEASURABLE, tool's own
      message, verbatim via --json.
UNBUILT (1): contracts/breach (decision 2) -- only .harness/design-T-436-
  contracts.md exists; no code to run.

Security self-check (acceptance criterion 1 + 6): script never imports blackboard/
precedent/deliberate/attest/reputation/currency/event_stats/westphalia_kpi (grep
confirms only stdlib imports); .harness/keys/ excluded from the copytree and never
referenced; no warrant.py draft/apply/sign call anywhere (trust/+constitutional/+
warrants/ are copied verbatim as already-operator-signed public material, same
treatment the task note sanctions for trust/constitutional); every agent key is a
fresh `ssh-keygen` call into the sandbox's own keys/ dir. No absolute user path
appears in either file (grep -n "<user>" examples/rehearsal/run_rehearsal.py
.harness/tests/test_rehearsal.py -> no output).

Please independently re-run both replay commands above and check the printed/
written scorecard against the prose claims, and sanity-check the D3a root-cause
claim against .harness/bin/attest.py's open_intents()/sign_act() if time allows.

VERIFIED (independent replay, different agent from producer worker-g9-rehearsal). Re-ran python3 examples/rehearsal/run_rehearsal.py fresh: fired=8 blocked=4 unbuilt=1, live .harness/ untouched: YES, exit 0 -- reproduces producer's reported scorecard exactly. Pre/post git status --porcelain and sha256 manifest of live .harness/ (excl logs/, task files) are byte-identical across the run; only logs/transcript.jsonl (gitignored, this session's own PostToolUse hook) differs. Opened the persisted sandbox tempdir myself (script does not delete it) and read raw tool-written files directly for every FIRED row: tasks/T-442.json (self-done refusal note + handoff + distinct-verifier done note), cases/C-004.json (status=disposed, disposal.verb=publish, ref=PR-064), deliberations/D-003.json (5 distinct final_ballots, condorcet_winner=fijar_regla, concluded_by=revision-mecanismo), precedents/PR-064.json (confirmation_status=confirmed, confirmed_by=registro-b, cited_by=[PR-065]), precedents/PR-065.json (relations=[{type:follows,target:PR-064}]), logs/events.jsonl line 17 ({event:phase_b_yield, agent:rehearsal-newcomer, outranked_by:registro-a}), acts/fed-codificador/002.json+003.json (prev hashes chain seq2->seq3 sequentially, confirming zero forks independent of attest.py forks' own report). Independently re-ran currency.py/event_stats.py/westphalia_kpi.py/attest.py forks directly against the sandbox and got matching output. Read attest.py's open_intents()/sign_act() source directly (static method, different from producer's dynamic probing) and confirmed the D3a PRIVILEGED_KINDS intent-gate is the real, singular root cause cited for all 4 blocked rows. Mutation testing in a THROWAWAY repo copy under the scratchpad (never the working tree): made 3 separate mutant copies and neutered one mechanism each -- (1) suppressed blackboard.py's phase_b_yield hc.log_event call -> that row flipped FIRED->BLOCKED ('no phase_b_yield event written'); (2) suppressed precedent.py's cited_by back-reference append on follows -> the second-case-citation row flipped FIRED->BLOCKED (cited_by=[]); (3) disabled blackboard.py's producer!=approver guard (both the no-handoff and same-producer refusal branches) -> the self-done call returned rc=0 and the row flipped FIRED->BLOCKED, with a correct cascading effect on the next row (handoff+distinct-verifier) since the task was already terminal. All 3 mutants confirm the scorecard is sensitive to real tool behavior, not hardcoded. Security: grepped script+test for 'warrant' (no CLI call to warrant.py anywhere), confirmed keys_dir always resolves to the sandbox's own harness_dir/keys (COPY_EXCLUDE_DIRS includes keys, verified by reading build_sandbox()), confirmed live .harness/keys/* and ~/.ssh/harness_root mtimes unchanged (Aug 16, predating this run) by direct ls -la, and grepped for the user's absolute path / username in both files (no matches). Full suite: python3 .harness/bin/goal_mode.py run --cmd 'python3 -m pytest .harness/tests -q' -> GOAL REACHED iteration 1/3 (80.44s). Read test_rehearsal.py directly: asserts sha256 tree equality + filtered git status equality + scorecard shape (fired needs evidence, non-fired needs blocker, all 3 outcome kinds present) -- matches what I replayed by hand. Verdict: T-440 acceptance criteria hold under independent replay and adversarial mutation. Housekeeping: lock.py status clean, lock.py sweep swept 0.
